items.note: Each capability entry under New Capabilities must name a kebab-case path (segments separated by /).

sources.quote: Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce (e.g., user-auth or identity/user-auth) ... - `<capability-path>`: <brief description of what this capability covers>

items.downgrade_reason: Delta specs for Modified Capabilities reuse existing paths, which may not be kebab-case; the rule only binds paths the agent introduces.

sources.quote: Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce ... Each creates specs/<capability-path>/spec.md.

items.note: Change directory must be changes/issue (or its archived {DATE}-issue form).

unitemized.reason: Unimplemented: to catch verbatim copying of the config's context/operationGuidance into files, the check would need the runtime CLI text, and no kind can compare against it.

Telling whether a capability name is really an implementation task takes judgment. The proposal's section headings, apart from 'New Capabilities', are not available as literals, so a disjointness check cannot be written verbatim.
The document gives no list of forbidden catch-all names (e.g. misc/general). Writing such a list would invent literals, and judging 'broad' is subjective.

Unimplemented: base_paths are full file paths (openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md), while proposal entries are bare capability paths. No selector or normalization can map one onto the other, so the subset check cannot be written.
This allows an empty Modified Capabilities section rather than requiring anything. Whether requirements are changing cannot be observed independently of the proposal.
Unimplemented: .openspec.yaml is not a declared artifact, and no predicate or kind can read its skip_specs value.
